title: セイバールート十三日目-00

pages.ja:
日が落ちて夜になった頃、雨はすっかり止んでいた。
朝の話通りなら、夕食を済ませた後は町に出てマスターを捜す事になるのだが

pages.en:
By the time the sun sets and night arrives, the rain has stopped completely.

If we follow the plan we discussed this morning, we will go into town after dinner and search for the remaining Masters. But before that——

セイバーの意思。
彼女が何を目的にして戦っているのかを。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“I need to make certain of something.”

Saber's intentions.

What purpose she has been fighting to achieve.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I have to find out before that.”
Saber’s intentions.
I need to know why she is fighting.

よし、と気合いを入れて立ち上がる。
とにかく居間に向かおう。
夕食前の穏やかな空気を盾に、セイバーの牙城をうち破れればいいのだが

pages.en:
“…Though asking her outright probably won't work. I'll have to draw it out of her as casually as I can.”

——All right.

I rise with renewed determination and head for the living room.

Perhaps the peaceful mood before dinner will give me enough cover to breach Saber's defenses.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…But I can’t ask her straight on… I have to try to ask her as indirectly as possible.”
I make my mind up and stand up.
Let’s go to the living room.
I hope I’ll be able to penetrate the fortress using the calm before-dinner air as a shield

pages.ja:
「例えばの話だけど。
もし聖杯戦争に勝ち残れたとしたら、どうしようか」
と。
色々考えてもいい案が浮かばなかったんで、単刀直入に切り出してみた。

「例えばの話だけど。
もし聖杯戦争に勝ち残れたとしたら、どうしようか」
と。

pages.en:
“Hypothetically speaking.

“What should we do if we survive the Holy Grail War and win?”

After considering every approach and finding none that seemed promising, I open with the question as bluntly as possible.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Just hypothetically.
What should we do if we win the Holy Grail War?”
So.
Since I couldn’t come up with any good ideas, I ask her directly.

pages.ja:
「え？」
「は？」
「ん？」
三者三様、異なる仕草でおんなじような反応をする。
pages.jaRuby:
「え？」
「は？」
「ん？」
三者三様、異なる仕草でおんなじような反応をする。
pages.en:
“What?”

“I beg your pardon?”

“Hm?”

Each responds in her own fashion, yet all three reactions mean exactly the same thing.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Eh?”
“Huh?”
“Hm?”
They all give the same response with different expressions.

pages.ja:
「
だから勝った後の事だよ。聖杯を手に入れたらどうするかって話」
pages.jaRuby:
「
だから勝った後の事だよ。聖杯を手に入れたらどうするかって話」
pages.en: “——I mean after we win. I'm asking what we'll do if we obtain the Holy Grail.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I’m talking about after we win. I’m saying what should we do if we win the Holy Grail War.”

pages.ja: 「そんなの説明されなくても分かるけど……どういう風の吹き回しよ。アンタがそんなコト言い出すなんて」
pages.jaRuby: 「そんなの説明されなくても分かるけど……どういう風の吹き回しよ。アンタがそんなコト言い出すなんて」
pages.en: “I understood you without the explanation… What brought this on? I never expected *you* to raise a subject like that.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “You don’t need to explain the question… but what’s wrong? Why are you asking?”

pages.ja:
頷きこそしないものの、セイバーとイリヤも同意見っぽい顔をしている。
……やっぱりいきなり切り出すのは不自然だったか。
けど、それでも今回はしらを切り通さなければ。

pages.en:
Neither Saber nor Illya nods, but their expressions plainly agree with her.

…Perhaps bringing it up so abruptly was suspicious after all.

Even so, this time I have to keep playing innocent.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Even though they don’t nod, it seems like Saber and Illya have the same question.
…I guess it was unnatural to abruptly ask.
But I have to play ignorant for now.

pages.ja:
「ああ、いや
ただの思い付きだ。
ほら、残ったサーヴァントはあと三人なんだから、そういうコト考えてもおかしくないだろ。数が減って、明白に終わりが見えてきたんだから」

pages.en:
“Oh, no—it just occurred to me.

“Look, only three Servants remain. It isn't strange to start thinking about the end now. Their numbers have fallen far enough that we can finally see it approaching.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well, it just came to mind.
There are only three Servants left, so it’s not that weird to start thinking about it, right? There’s not much left now and the end is near.”

pages.ja:
「ふーん……ま、言われてみればそうよね。
いくら士郎だって、この状況ならそれぐらいは考えるか。好きで始めたコトじゃないって言っても、命を張ってる以上は報酬ぐらい気になるだろうし」
pages.jaRuby:
「ふーん……ま、言われてみればそうよね。
いくら士郎だって、この状況ならそれぐらいは考えるか。好きで始めたコトじゃないって言っても、命を張ってる以上は報酬ぐらい気になるだろうし」
pages.en:
“Hmm… Well, when you put it that way, you're right.

“Even you would give it some thought under the circumstances. You may not have entered this willingly, but if your life is at stake, naturally you'd wonder about the reward.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hmm… Well, you’re right.
Even you’ll start thinking about it in this situation. Even though you didn’t start this because you wanted to, I bet you’re curious about the reward since you’re risking your life.”

pages.ja:
「そ、そうそう。一応それぐらいは考える」
……遠坂が理屈好きで助かった。
話に筋が通っていれば、それも可能性の一つとして考慮するのが遠坂のいいトコロだと思う。
とりあえず、この瞬間だけの話だが。
pages.jaRuby:

話に筋が通っていれば、それも可能性の一つとして考慮するのが遠坂のいいトコロだと思う。

pages.en:
“Y-yes, exactly. I've at least thought that much.”

…Thank goodness Tohsaka likes things to make logical sense.

One of her better qualities is that if a proposition holds together, she will at least admit it as a possibility.

For this particular moment, anyway.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Y-Yeah. I’m curious.”
…Thank God Tohsaka likes to reason things out.
I think one of Tohsaka’s good aspects is to consider anything as a possibility if it sounds reasonable.
Well, just in this case, though.

pages.ja:
「それで、遠坂はどうなんだよ。もし聖杯が手に入ったらどうするんだ？」
出来るだけ自然に問いかける。
pages.jaRuby:
「それで、遠坂はどうなんだよ。もし聖杯が手に入ったらどうするんだ？」
出来るだけ自然に問いかける。
pages.en:
“So what about you, Tohsaka? What will you do if you obtain the Holy Grail?”

I make the question sound as natural as I can.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So, how about you, Tohsaka? What will you do if you get the Holy Grail?”
I ask as naturally as I can.

pages.ja:
「……そうね。わたしは勝つ事しか考えてなかったから、聖杯に叶えて貰うような目的はないわ。
とりあえず聖杯を手に入れるけど、その後のコトは考えてなかったな」

「……そうね。わたしは勝つ事しか考えてなかったから、聖杯に叶えて貰うような目的はないわ。

pages.en:
“…Let me see. I've thought only about winning, so I don't have any particular wish for the Grail to grant.

“I'll obtain it, of course, but I haven't considered what to do after that.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Let’s see. I only really thought about winning, so there’s nothing I wanted the Holy Grail to grant.
I’ll get it, but I haven’t thought about anything after that.”

pages.en:
“————”

So she fights because she refuses to lose.

…Well, I had assumed as much. I simply never imagined that would truly be the whole of it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
So she’s fighting because she doesn’t want to lose, huh?
…Well, I guessed so, but I never really thought I’d be right.

pages.ja:
「呆れた。いちばん物を考えていそうで、実はいちばん考えてないのよね、リンは」
「ふん、言うじゃない。じゃあそういうアンタはどうなのよ、イリヤスフィール」

「ふん、言うじゃない。じゃあそういうアンタはどうなのよ、イリヤスフィール」
pages.en:
“Unbelievable. Rin looks as though she thinks more than anyone, when really she thinks less than anyone.”

“Hmph. Bold words. What about you, then, Illyasviel?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’m stunned. You seem to be the one thinking the most, but you’re actually the one who thinks the least.”
“Heh, you’re one to talk. Then what about you, Illyasviel?”

pages.ja:
「そんなの知らない。聖杯はわたしのだから、誰にも渡すなって言われただけよ。
もともとわたしの物なんだから、そんなものに興味あるわけないじゃない」
pages.jaRuby:
「そんなの知らない。聖杯はわたしのだから、誰にも渡すなって言われただけよ。
もともとわたしの物なんだから、そんなものに興味あるわけないじゃない」
pages.en:
“I don't know. I was only told that the Holy Grail belongs to me and that I must never surrender it to anyone.

“It was mine to begin with. Why would I be interested in it?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I don’t know. I was just told that the Holy Grail is mine, so I shouldn’t give it to anyone.
Since it’s mine to begin with, of course I don’t care about it.”

pages.ja:
「……ふうん。ようするに聖杯より聖杯戦争の方が楽しいってコト？」
「当然よ。わたしは勝つためだけに来たんだもの。聖杯の使い道なんてどうでもいいわ」
pages.jaRuby:
「……ふうん。ようするに聖杯より聖杯戦争の方が楽しいってコト？」
「当然よ。わたしは勝つためだけに来たんだもの。聖杯の使い道なんてどうでもいいわ」
pages.en:
“…I see. So you find the Holy Grail War more interesting than the Grail itself?”

“Of course. I came here for the sole purpose of winning. I don't care how the Grail is used.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Oh. So you’re saying the Holy Grail War is more fun than the Holy Grail?”
“Of course. I only came to win. I don’t care who uses the Holy Grail.”

pages.ja:
……似たもの同士、というのか。
二人は何を言うでもなく、むむ、とお互いを睨み、なんともいえないシンパシーを得ているようだ。

pages.en:
…Two of a kind, perhaps.

Without a word, they trade fierce little glares. Somehow, the two seem to have found an indefinable kinship.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Are they the same?
The two glare at each other silently and there seems to be a sympathy I can’t understand.

But however much Saber may dislike it, I have to ask this question now.

pages.en:
“I think I understand what the two of you want.”

I nod as casually as I can.

“What about you, Saber?”

I turn to the one person who has kept her silence.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I kind of understand you two’s intentions.”
I try to nod naturally and…
“Then how about you, Saber?”
I ask Saber.

pages.en:
“…………………………”

Saber does not answer.

…Tohsaka and Illya must sense that something is wrong. They end their quarrel and turn toward her as well.

Measured by the clock, the silence may last a full minute.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……”
Saber doesn’t answer.
…They must have realized Saber’s acting in a complicated manner as they both stare at her.
If I’m counting, there must be about a minute’s silence.

「今更語るまでもありませんが、聖杯を手に入れるのは私の義務です。
聖杯がどれほどの許容範囲を持っているかは知らない。
ですがそれが聖杯である限り、私は聖杯を手に入れなくてはなりません。
……そして無論、聖杯が私の望みを叶えられるなら、望みを叶えるだけですが」

pages.en:
“There should be no need to say it again, but it is my duty to obtain the Holy Grail.

“I do not know the limits of what the Grail can grant.

“But so long as it is the Holy Grail, I must possess it.

“…And naturally, if it can grant my wish, I will ask it to do so.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I do not need to say this, but it is my duty to obtain the Holy Grail.
I do not know how powerful the Holy Grail is.
But as long as it is the Holy Grail, I must obtain it.
…And of course, I would have my wish granted if it can grant it.”

！

——She said it.

Saber has confirmed that she possesses a wish of her own——!
pages.mirrorMoon:
She said it.
Without a doubt, Saber said she has her own wish!

pages.en:
“I see. So what is that wish?”

I hold down my pounding heart and ask with every appearance of calm.

“————”

Saber does not answer.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. Then what’s your wish?”
I restrain my pounding heart and ask calmly.
“”
Saber doesn’t answer.

pages.ja:
……それならそれでいい。
答えられない、というのなら、それは利己的なコトっていう可能性が高い。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
…Then perhaps that is enough.

If she cannot bring herself to answer, there is a good chance that her wish is selfish.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…That’s fine too.
If she cannot answer, chances are good that her wish is a selfish one.

pages.en:
Knowing Saber, she would hesitate to speak aloud a desire meant for herself alone.

So perhaps it is better that she remain silent than name some absurd wish.

That fainthearted hope occupies my thoughts.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Considering Saber’s personality, she would hesitate to speak of a selfish wish.
SoI would prefer if she keep quiet and not tell me a ridiculous wish.
Such whining fills my head.

サーヴァントの望みは現世に蘇る事だってお爺さまは言ってたわ。英霊たちは二度目の生を得るために聖杯を求めるんだって。セイバーだってそうじゃないの？」

pages.en:
“What? Is it really so difficult?

“Grandfather told me that a Servant's wish is to return to life in this world. Heroic Spirits seek the Holy Grail so that they can receive a second life. Isn't that true for you too, Saber?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Is it that hard?
Grandfather said the wish of the Servants is to be resurrected into this world. Those Servants seek the Holy Grail to live a second life. Isn’t that the case for you, Saber?”

その言葉に、思わず顔をあげた。
それがセイバーの望みなら、なんの問題もない。
だが、それは。

I look up without meaning to.

If that is Saber's wish, there is nothing wrong with it.

But——
pages.mirrorMoon:
I raise my head at her words.
There’s no problem if that’s Saber’s wish.
But…

もともとこの身は、聖杯を手に入れる代償として、サーヴァントになったのですから」

“My sole purpose is to obtain the Holy Grail.

The woman who took up that holy sword—that oath—could never have sought a second life for herself.

I knew that had to be it.
I knew the girl who took that oath pulling out the sword would not seek a second life.
